turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, nice to meet you, Doctor. I'm here because... well, ever since my choir friend passed away so suddenly, I just haven't been myself. 

I find myself crying over little things, like looking at the potluck lists. And I get all worked up about phone calls that I used to handle easy. I've even started missing church planning meetings... and I never would have missed those before. I just feel like I'm having a really hard time managing right now.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient reports developing emotional and behavioral difficulties—including tearfulness, anxiety over routine tasks, and missing church commitments—specifically following the sudden death of a choir friend.

turns.doctor_question: How long ago did your friend pass away, and how long have you been feeling this way since then?
turns.patient_response: Well, she passed away just about a month ago. It was... a very sudden loss. And I've been feeling this way pretty much ever since then. It was really only after she died that I started falling apart with the church planning and everything else. Before that, I was managing just fine.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient describes developing emotional and functional difficulties ('falling apart') directly in response to the identifiable stressor of their friend's sudden death one month ago.

turns.doctor_question: Over the past month, have you noticed that you feel down or find little interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, nearly every day, even outside of situations that remind you of your friend?
turns.patient_response:
Well, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean... I still enjoy things when my mind isn't on her. I still like working out in my yard, and I enjoy seeing my family. 

It's not an all-day, every-day kind of sadness about everything in my life. It really just hits me hard when something reminds me of her, or when I have to deal with the church stuff we used to do together. Outside of that, I feel mostly okay.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies persistent, pervasive depressed mood, stating it is not an all-day, every-day sadness and that they feel mostly okay outside of specific reminders.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient denies loss of interest or pleasure, stating they still enjoy activities like working in their yard and seeing family.

turns.doctor_question: Besides feeling sad or tearful, have you also been feeling unusually anxious, nervous, or on edge since your friend passed away?
turns.patient_response: Well, I wouldn't say I've been feeling unusually anxious or nervous, really. It's more just the sadness and getting overwhelmed with the church things. But I don't feel on edge or anything like that in my day-to-day life.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient confirms experiencing ongoing sadness following the loss of their friend.
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient explicitly denies feeling unusually nervous or on edge in their day-to-day life.
